title: Draw a pan from the back of a deep oven with the peel, then lift it out
instruction: The baking pan at the back of the oven is too far in to reach. Take the wooden peel, slide its blade between the two steel runners under the pan, raise it to lift the pan off the runners, and draw the pan forward to the oven mouth. Set the pan back down on the runners there, take the peel out and lay it on the table. Then lift the pan out of the oven and put it on the white pass pad.
context: Deck and pizza ovens are deeper than an arm can safely reach: bakers and cooks are taught never to reach across a hot deck, and use a long peel to bring a pan or loaf to the mouth before taking it out with a gloved hand. The skill is tool use for reach: the tool has to go under the load and lift it clear before drawing it, then be put away before the load is handled directly. Unlike ManiSkill3 PullCubeTool, where a hook drags a cube within reach, and TK-92EVR5, where a spatula pulls a part out from under a guard, here the peel must lift the pan off its runners, carry it forward level, set it back down, and come out before the pan is lifted out by hand. Done by: restaurant cooks and bakers (O*NET 35-2014.00, 51-3011.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Oven: a fixed dark deck 30 cm deep, 18 cm wide, 3 cm tall, its front edge at x 40, centred on y 30, with fixed side walls 1 cm thick and 10 cm tall 15 cm apart and a back wall at x 70. Runners: two fixed steel bars 28 x 1 x 3.6 cm along x on the deck, from x 41, centred at y 35.3 and 24.7. Pan: a loose dark grey box 7 cm deep (x) by 12 cm wide by 3 cm tall, 80 g, resting on both runners at x 60, y 30. Peel: a loose wooden board 21.5 cm long (x), 6 cm wide, 1.6 cm thick, 90 g, flat on the table centred at x 25, y 16. Pass pad: a fixed white pad 16 x 16 cm, 4 mm thick, centred at x 22, y 43.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses, with the grippers open at the end. 0.25 once the pan has been drawn 6 cm forward; 0.5 at 12 cm; 0.75 with the pan's centre out of the oven (in front of the deck's edge); 1.0 with the pan level (under 5 degrees) and at rest on the pass pad, its centre within 3.5 cm of the pad's centre, and the peel wholly out of the oven and at rest on the table. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: score 1, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the pan back on the runners at the back of the deck and lay the peel on its mark; the deck, walls, runners and pass pad do not move.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The oven is drawn without its roof and door so the cameras see in, and nothing is hot. The peel is one flat board with no tapered edge, so it slides under the pan between the runners rather than scooping it off the deck. The pan is a plain box with no food or rim.
